chapter: California, New York and Richard Himber
title: Himber's audition and the union fixer Jack Rosenberg
summary: Himber auditioned Hirsch on vibes, Local 802's president Rosenberg arranged the union side, and he played radio opens and dinner sets.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: He says, can you read music? I said, yeah. He says, can you fake music? I said, yes. He says, can you fake music? I said, yes. He says, go play something for me. I said, I can't. I said, the piano player's playing. Art was playing the piano. We'll go over there and tell him to play something and let you play with him. So I said, alright. So I went over there. I said, alright. I said, you want to accompany me for playing something? Yeah, yeah. I said, go ahead and play. So we started playing. After I got finished, I went over to him and went, okay, see me at my office. So I got to be a big romance with seeing him at his office and so forth and so on. And it was just about to open at the Essex house. He lived at the Essex house. And then the union got on him about me because we got five players here that are not working. He says, if you don't come with me, he says, you ain't going to have no band in here. And he told him that Jack Rosenberg. And I knew Jack Rosenberg too. My daddy knew Jack Rosenberg. My daddy was a member of, he used to go to conventions and got to know Rosenberg. So Jack could fix up things. So he fixed it up. The only thing I could do, I couldn't do the TV show or the radio shows because you had two radio shows. One on the red network and one on the blue network and the NBC. And I couldn't do the radio shows but I could do the radio show from there. Because him always used an opening with the vibes. I'd go, ding dong, ding dong dong, ding. And he was, so I worked the dinner show with the harp player. We used to play harp and vibra harp for dinner music. And then at night, I'd come in and I'd do the radio show. I had a schedule. I was in and out and I didn't know what the hell it went on. And that's when I went with Dick. Ron Lee ended up managing his band. And we became very good friends. Very close friends.
What did Rosenberg do? Was he a...
He fixed it up so that I could...
Is he a lawyer or just a...
No, he was the president of 802. Oh, yeah.
